extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to the Annals of Statistics (statisticians/researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting research manuscripts to the Annals of Statistics, including formatting, submission procedure, length, affiliations, acknowledgements, and supplemental material rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission declaration (originality and exclusivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a paper implies (a) that the same work has not been published before; (b) that it is not under consideration for publication elsewhere; and (c) that its publication has been approved by all co-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a condition of submission—ensure prior publication and simultaneous submission constraints are respected and obtain co-author approval prior to submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission via EJMS
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions to Annals of Statistics must be made electronically through the IMS’s Electronic Journal Management System (EJMS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should access https://www.e-publications.org/ims/submission/. First-time users must complete registration (only once). As a registered user, you will have the ability to upload your manuscript as a PDF file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee suggestions and contact policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If desired, you may use the “Comments to the editor” box to suggest referees who are experts in fields relevant for the submitted paper with the understanding that the editors, along with the associate editors, may or may not choose to utilize the suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do not canvass or directly contact the suggested referees about your paper. Editors may ignore or use suggestions at their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required source format and template (LaTeX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must be written in LaTeX using AOS’s template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template will set proper margins and font. sample.pdf and sample.tex files will assist in the preparation of a camera-ready paper in LaTeX. These documents contain useful information regarding the structure of your document, proper tagging style, layout features, etc. Please do not use any packages or commands that affect the layout or formatting of your document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length guideline and use of Supplementary Material
rubrics_metrics.description: A typical paper should not exceed 25 pages using the standard style files from the Annals of Statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more space is needed, additional material (such as further technical derivations or more detailed simulation results) should be placed as Supplementary Material; follow the linked Supplement Instructions for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliations and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Please list one affiliation per author (department and university only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an author has more than one affiliation, the others should be listed in the Acknowledgments section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement policy (what to include)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgements should be limited to referencing: (a) named individuals who have contributed to the research by providing tangible inputs such as ideas, feedback, or code, (b) possibly-anonymous individuals who have served in the paper’s evaluation via the refereeing and editorial process, (c) organizations that provided funding, and/or (d) scientific institutions or meetings where the research was conducted or facilitated, if other than the home institution of an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep acknowledgements focused on tangible contributions, evaluation participants, funding organizations, and outside institutions/meetings; avoid unrelated or excessive acknowledgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Material submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If your paper has supplemental material please follow the instructions (linked).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary material is the appropriate place for extended technical derivations, additional simulation results, and other material exceeding the main paper length; authors must follow the journal’s Supplement Instructions for formatting and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter template layout or formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use any packages or commands that affect the layout or formatting of your document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on the provided template to set margins, fonts, and layout; altering layout-affecting packages/commands can violate submission requirements and interfere with production.
